concepts.name: CSO: Institutional Identity, Merger into NSO, and Current Status
key_dimensions: CSO's merger with NSSO to form the National Statistical Office (NSO) in 2019 under MoSPI
Distinction between NSO (operational body) and NSC (National Statistical Commission — advisory/oversight body)
UPSC trap: CSO no longer exists as a standalone entity; questions may still use 'CSO' as a label
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) as the nodal ministry

concepts.name: National Accounts Statistics (NAS): GDP Estimation Methodology
key_dimensions: Three approaches: Production/Output, Expenditure, and Income methods — CSO/NSO uses production and expenditure approaches
Base year revisions: shift from 2004-05 to 2011-12 base year and controversies around rebasing
GDP vs. GVA distinction: GDP = GVA + Net Taxes on Products
UPSC trap: India uses GVA at basic prices (not market prices) as the primary measure of sectoral output

concepts.name: Advance, Revised, and Final GDP Estimates: Release Calendar and Accuracy
key_dimensions: First Advance Estimate (FAE) released in January of the same fiscal year, used for Union Budget preparation
Second Advance Estimate (SAE) released in February; followed by Provisional and then Final Estimates
Criticism of FAE accuracy: limited data availability leads to revisions — policy implications
UPSC trap: FAE is released before the fiscal year ends, making it an estimate, not actual data

concepts.name: Index of Industrial Production (IIP): Compilation and Significance
key_dimensions: IIP compiled by CSO/NSO; base year currently 2011-12
Three-sector classification: Mining, Manufacturing, Electricity — and Use-based classification (capital goods, consumer durables, etc.)
Monthly release with a 6-week lag; subject to revision
UPSC trap: IIP measures volume/quantum of industrial output, NOT value — distinguishing it from GDP contribution

concepts.name: Consumer Price Index (CPI): CSO's Role and Architecture
key_dimensions: CSO releases CPI (Combined), CPI (Urban), and CPI (Rural) — base year 2012
Distinction: CSO compiles CPI; Labour Bureau compiles CPI-IW (Industrial Workers) and CPI-AL (Agricultural Labourers)
CPI (Combined) is the headline inflation measure used by RBI for monetary policy under inflation targeting framework
UPSC trap: WPI is compiled by Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT), NOT CSO/NSO

concepts.name: Wholesale Price Index (WPI) vs. CPI: Institutional Ownership and Differences
key_dimensions: WPI: compiled by Office of Economic Adviser under DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce); base year 2011-12
CPI: compiled by NSO/CSO under MoSPI; used for RBI inflation targeting
WPI covers only goods (no services); CPI covers goods and services consumed by households
UPSC trap: RBI switched from WPI to CPI as its inflation anchor in 2014 — many questions test this transition

concepts.name: National Statistical Commission (NSC): Composition, Powers, and Relationship with NSO
key_dimensions: NSC set up in 2006 on recommendations of Rangarajan Commission; not a statutory body — set up by Cabinet Resolution
Functions: oversight of core statistics, coordination among statistical agencies, approval of statistical standards
NSC vs. NSO: NSC is advisory/oversight; NSO is the operational arm under MoSPI
UPSC trap: NSC is NOT a constitutional or statutory body — it cannot compel compliance; this is a recurring trap

concepts.name: Collection of Statistics Act, 2008: Legal Framework for Official Statistics
key_dimensions: Provides legal backing to the Central Government and State Governments to collect statistical information
Mandates responses from households/establishments — non-compliance is punishable
Amended in 2017 to include States and UTs more explicitly
UPSC trap: This is the ONLY legislation specifically governing statistical data collection in India — distinguishes India's framework from purely administrative setups

concepts.name: Sectoral Classification of GDP: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary and their Measurement
key_dimensions: CSO/NSO classifies economy into Agriculture & allied (Primary), Industry (Secondary), Services (Tertiary)
GVA at basic prices used for sectoral estimates; taxes and subsidies on products added to get GDP
Services sector contributes ~55% of GDP — measurement challenges due to informal nature
UPSC trap: Construction is classified under Industry (Secondary sector), NOT Services — a common error

concepts.name: Per Capita Income (PNI per Capita): Estimation and Policy Use
key_dimensions: CSO/NSO releases Per Capita Net National Income (NNI) at current and constant prices as India's per capita income
Distinction: GNP vs. NNP vs. NNI — NNI = NNP at factor cost (historically); now NNI = GNI - CCA
Used for determining eligibility for international financial classifications (e.g., World Bank income categories)
UPSC trap: India's official 'per capita income' figure refers to Per Capita NNI, not Per Capita GDP

concepts.name: Gross Value Added (GVA) vs. GDP: Conceptual Distinction and UPSC Relevance
key_dimensions: GVA at basic prices = GDP at market prices − Net taxes on products (taxes minus subsidies on products)
Post-2011-12 base year revision, India shifted to GVA at basic prices as the primary production-side measure
Sectoral GVA growth rates can differ significantly from overall GDP growth rate
UPSC trap: Subsidies on products (like food/fertilizer subsidies routed through product prices) REDUCE the gap between GVA and GDP

concepts.name: Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS): NSO's Labour Statistics Framework
key_dimensions: PLFS launched in 2017 by NSO replacing the older NSSO Employment-Unemployment Survey (EUS)
Provides quarterly urban data and annual rural+urban data on employment, unemployment, and labour force participation
Key metrics: LFPR (Labour Force Participation Rate), WPR (Worker Population Ratio), UR (Unemployment Rate)
UPSC trap: PLFS is conducted by NSO (erstwhile NSSO wing), NOT a private agency — and it replaced EUS, not the Census

concepts.name: Economic Census: Scope, Frequency, and Distinction from Population Census
key_dimensions: Economic Census conducted by CSO/NSO in collaboration with State Directorates of Economics & Statistics
Covers all non-farm entrepreneurial units — NOT agricultural operations (those are covered by Agriculture Census under MoA)
Seventh Economic Census (2019) was conducted digitally in partnership with CSC e-Governance Services
UPSC trap: Economic Census does NOT cover agricultural activities and is NOT conducted by the Registrar General of India (who conducts Population Census)

concepts.name: Base Year Revision in National Accounts: Rationale, Process, and Controversies
key_dimensions: Base year shifted from 2004-05 to 2011-12 in January 2015 — changed methodology (GVA at basic prices, MCA21 corporate data)
Controversy: new series showed higher GDP growth rates for UPA years, leading to political and academic debate
Back-series data controversy: NITI Aayog's back-series (2004-2017) conflicted with NSC's back-series estimates
UPSC trap: Base year revision changes BOTH the level and growth rate of GDP — not just the base price level

concepts.name: Rangarajan Commission on Statistics: Recommendations and Implementation
key_dimensions: Set up in 2000; recommended creation of a permanent, autonomous National Statistical Commission
Key recommendation: separation of data collection (NSSO) from data compilation/analysis (CSO) under an umbrella NSC
Led to establishment of NSC in 2006 and later the formal merger of CSO+NSSO into NSO in 2019
UPSC trap: NSC was NOT recommended to be a statutory body — it remains a non-statutory body, which limits its enforcement powers

concepts.name: India's Compliance with UN System of National Accounts (SNA 2008)
key_dimensions: India progressively aligns national accounts with UN SNA 2008 standards — the 2011-12 base year revision was a step toward this
Key SNA 2008 changes adopted: treatment of R&D as capital formation, financial intermediation services indirectly measured (FISIM)
Challenges: large informal economy, data gaps in unorganized sector make full SNA compliance difficult
UPSC trap: India does NOT fully comply with SNA 2008 yet — it is a work in progress, distinguishing India from advanced economies

concepts.name: Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES): Status, Suppression Controversy, and Revival
key_dimensions: Conducted periodically by NSO (erstwhile NSSO); last officially released survey was 2011-12 (68th Round)
2017-18 survey results were withheld by the government amid controversy over data quality and reported decline in consumption
2022-23 HCES was released in February 2024 — first official release in over a decade
UPSC trap: HCES is distinct from PLFS (labour) and NFHS (health/nutrition) — it specifically measures household consumption patterns used for poverty estimation and CPI basket revision

concepts.name: Informal/Unorganized Sector Measurement: Methodological Challenges for CSO/NSO
key_dimensions: Unorganized sector estimated using benchmark-indicator method — lacks direct enterprise-level data
NSSO Enterprise Surveys and Economic Census serve as benchmarks; outdated benchmarks distort GDP estimates
COVID-19 exposed measurement gaps: formal GDP data captured decline in organized sector but underestimated informal sector collapse
UPSC trap: India's GDP estimates for the unorganized sector are largely IMPUTED, not directly measured — a fundamental methodological limitation

concepts.name: MCA21 Corporate Database: Role in New GDP Estimation Methodology
key_dimensions: Post-2011-12 base year revision, NSO uses Ministry of Corporate Affairs' MCA21 database for corporate sector GDP estimation
Replaced the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) as the primary data source for organized manufacturing
Controversy: MCA21 data includes shell companies and inactive firms, potentially inflating corporate sector GVA
UPSC trap: MCA21 database covers ONLY registered companies — it does NOT capture proprietorships, partnerships, or informal enterprises

concepts.name: State Domestic Product (SDP/GSDP): Estimation by States vs. CSO Coordination Role
key_dimensions: GSDP is estimated by individual State Directorates of Economics & Statistics (DES), NOT directly by NSO/CSO
CSO issues guidelines and methodological standards to ensure comparability across states
GSDP data used for fiscal federalism (Finance Commission devolution), CRISIL/RBI state rankings, and planning
UPSC trap: Summation of all GSDPs does NOT equal national GDP — due to differences in methodology, coverage of central government activities, and inter-state flows
